visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 accurately shows the binary search states, highlighted indices, discarded halves, found target, and O(log n) shrinkage, while Lesson 2 skips/misplaces key middle checks after the first comparison, prematurely highlights index 7, has overlapping low/high/mid markers, and even displays an unrelated target-40 prompt during the complexity section.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 has a well-formed, wired quiz gate after act_found with a real question, plausible options, and a marked correct answer, while Lesson 1 provides no gate specs or plan at all, so its interactivity is absent.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 has more natural, well-segmented narration with spoken math rendered clearly, while Lesson 1 is clear but denser and more repetitive, with less apparent pacing structure and slightly clunkier phrases like “Big O of Log N.”

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides mostly timed visual cues near the narrated references despite a few early cues, while Lesson 1 has no beat/timing cue data at all, so its many described visual changes cannot be verified as synchronized and are effectively unsupported on this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 gives a fully accurate, explicit trace of every binary-search comparison and the halving idea, while Lesson 2 is mostly correct but is less transparent about the middle steps and contains an accuracy inconsistency by saying in the plan that linear search would take 7 steps even though the correct comparison count is 8.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 is generally cleaner, larger, and more visually polished despite a few offscreen/empty-space moments, while Lesson 2 has smaller cramped text, visible raw backticks/formatting artifacts, overlapping labels, and a more cluttered off-center split layout.

aggregator.explanation: The dimension votes are split 3-3, but Lesson 1 has the stronger weighted case overall. It wins visual_accuracy and polish with very high confidence and concept_accuracy with solid confidence, indicating a cleaner, more accurate binary search trace and better visual execution. Lesson 2 clearly wins interactivity and also has advantages in narration and sync, but its visual and conceptual issues are significant. Given the slightly higher confidence-weighted support for Lesson 1, especially on accuracy-related dimensions, Lesson 1 is the overall winner.
